info.description: Rules-based tools for the US rental move-out. Property turnover prices the make-ready work from inspection findings, scaled to the ZIP code's labor market. Deposit settlement applies each state's security deposit statute (and covered cities' ordinances): the return deadline, each deduction assessed, interest, the refund and a draft itemized statement. Every result carries its citations, assumptions and the ruleset version that produced it. No account is needed. The same operations are MCP tools at /mcp/rental-property, and /catalog.json lists each one with its schemas and examples.

post.summary: Settle a security deposit after move-out
post.description:
Security deposit settlement for a US rental under the state's statute (and a covered city's ordinance): the date to return the deposit and itemized statement, each intended deduction assessed (allowed or not, prorated by useful life, documentation needed), interest owed, refund due, penalty exposure, a draft itemized statement and a citation for every rule. Covers all 50 states and DC, with city overlays for Chicago, San Francisco, Berkeley, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Minneapolis and Saint Paul.
When to use: A landlord or property manager is closing a move-out and asks when the deposit must be returned, what they may deduct (carpet, paint, cleaning, unpaid rent), how much interest is owed, what to put in the itemized statement, or what happens if they are late.
Not for: Not legal advice and not a tenant demand letter. It does not price repairs (use property_turnover_quick_estimate for that), hold or account for deposits, or cover pet deposits, last-month's rent handling or non-US rentals. Where the statute sets no deadline (Kentucky, Tennessee) it says so; never present a guessed date as the rule.
Tip: Send as_of (today's date) for a repeatable answer; it defaults to today in UTC.
Tip: Give item_installed_on or item_age_years for carpet, paint, blinds and appliances; without them the tenancy length is assumed.
Tip: Mark normal wear with caused_by_tenant false; it is never deductible.
Tip: Relay deadline.return_by and its status, totals.refund_due_usd, penalty_exposure and the citations with their links (citations[].url); relay the result's disclaimer word for word.
Tip: Offer statement.text as the draft itemized statement (no names or addresses); in the copy for the tenant keep only the statement.notes whose audience is tenant.
Tip: For a printable statement to sign and send (HTML or PDF) or the deductions ledger (CSV), POST the same arguments as JSON to links.downloads; do not build the file yourself.
Tip: For a tenant, links.downloads tenant_pdf or tenant_html is a neutral summary of the facts and the rule to send to the landlord; give the user that, not the landlord's statement. Send returned in its arguments (what came back and when, or nothing yet); without it the summary's "Returned so far" line says "Not stated".
Tip: Relay warnings, assumptions and unknowns (for example the Texas forwarding address).
Tip: Send the start-event dates a state needs when known (forwarding_address_received_on, demand_received_on, new_tenant_moved_in_on, claim_notice_sent_on in Florida); without them the clock is not_started.
Tip: Send the state-only facts the unknowns name (owner_is_natural_person in Georgia, county and deposit_in_separate_account in Tennessee, renter_notice_served_on in Utah, landlord_filed_action_on in Michigan).
Tip: deadline.status none_in_statute means no statutory deadline; deadline.extended_to is the statute's weekend roll-forward, but advise acting by return_by.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability deposit-settlement v0.1.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Quick turnover estimate (start here)
post.description:
The easiest way to estimate a US rental turnover: a ZIP, bedrooms, bathrooms and a list of plain-English issues in, a priced make-ready estimate out (same engine and result as property_turnover_scope, short summary by default).
When to use: Start here when the user describes a move-out or turnover in words ("carpet stained in both bedrooms, oven filthy") and wants a cost estimate or what to tell vendors. Use property_turnover_scope instead for rate cards, owner decisions, measured quantities or per-finding control.
Not for: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
Tip: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.
Tip: Relay refer_outs first, then the totals; say the numbers are estimates, not quotes.
Tip: When review.status is draft, show the user what was read (reading.findings) before you quote a number, and ask them to confirm or correct it. For a verified answer, send the confirmed findings to property_turnover_scope with confirmed true on each. A review.note says what was not read and why; with the AI reader unavailable only exact item names are priced.
Tip: From photos, list only what is visible, with its room ("stained carpet in bedroom 2"). Hedge doubtful ones ("possible water stain?") and ask the user about what photos cannot show: working appliances, odors, pests, sizes. Never state that a tenant caused damage because of a photo.
The same findings under the same ruleset return the same result_hash. An AI model may read notes into findings, marked for review (review, reading); it never sets a number. Capability property-turnover v1.0.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Scope a property turnover
post.description:
Turn move-out / turnover inspection findings for a US rental unit into a priced make-ready scope: standardized tasks by trade, regional low/expected/high costs, must/should/could priorities, vendor scopes, refer-outs to licensed professionals, and every assumption stated.
When to use: Turnover findings for a US rental unit when you need control: rooms, measured quantities, the manager's own prices (rate_card) or owner approve/decline decisions. For a plain-English estimate, property_turnover_quick_estimate is easier.
Not for: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
Tip: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.
Tip: From photos, describe only what is visible, with its room; an issue code only if one clearly fits, else general.manual_quote with your words in source_text. Hedge doubtful ones ("possible", "?") and ask the user about what photos cannot show: working appliances, odors, pests, sizes. Never state that a tenant caused damage because of a photo; responsibility stays a hint from the engine. Send no faces, names or addresses. A photo of a written checklist or report is different, so transcribe it as written.
Tip: Send a code on every finding, from property_turnover_issue_codes (search with q, read not_when), with the original words in source_text; general.manual_quote when no code fits. One code per condition; rooms as sets with counts ({"area": "bedroom", "count": 3}); status done, ok or none from the words; only evidence (a test result) clears a hazard. An unknown code is refused with the closest codes. A finding with no code is deprecated: until the date in deprecation it is a manual quote (not priced) whose words are still scanned for safety checks; read is ignored. For free text, use property_turnover_quick_estimate.
Tip: To confirm an AI reading, send the findings from reading.findings (keep each one's extraction, correct any the user changes) with confirmed true on each one the user checked. The answer is then verified and still shows which findings were read by AI.
Tip: Give measured quantities when you have them (e.g. 120 sq_ft); otherwise typical sizes are assumed and listed in assumptions.
Tip: Send property.floor_coverings when you know whether there is carpet, and unit_type single_family for houses; both change the baseline scope.
Tip: Relay the summary, refer_outs, assumptions and unknowns to the user; costs are estimate ranges, not quotes.
Tip: Use detail=summary unless the user asks for every line item (summary already lists every line tied to a finding).
Tip: Rate card examples - {"trade": "handyman", "unit_price": 65, "uom": "hour"} or {"task_id": "carpet.clean", "unit_price": 0.2, "uom": "sq_ft"}; check rate_card_applied and rate_card_ignored before saying a rate was used.
Tip: For the Excel workbook or owner estimate, give the user links.web_tool_prefilled (opens the free web tool with these findings) or POST the same arguments to links.downloads; do not build a spreadsheet yourself.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v1.0.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Look up turnover issue codes
post.description:
The issue-code catalog for rental-unit turnover (group.issue codes such as carpet.pet_urine): list every code, or search by words for full detail.
When to use: While preparing findings for a turnover cost estimate, to map each observed condition to one code before sending it to scope. Search with q for the detail (description, aliases, when not to use it, examples); call with no arguments for the short list of every code. Never needed to answer a question.
Not for: Legal or security-deposit questions; anything outside rental turnover and make-ready work. Not needed before quick_estimate, which reads plain words.
Tip: Map each observed condition to one code; search with q when unsure, and read not_when.
Tip: When no code fits, send general.manual_quote and keep the original words.
Tip: Call with no arguments for the short list of every code and the groups.
Deterministic: the same input returns the same result_hash. Capability property-turnover v1.0.0 (experimental).

post.summary: Read a document into findings (no estimate)
post.description:
Reads a move-out inspection report (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or CSV) or up to 5 photos of paper pages, 5 pages at most, and returns what it read as findings: a `reading`, never an estimate. Check each finding against its evidence (page and quote), then send `reading.findings` unchanged to `POST /v1/property-turnover/scope`, which prices them by our own rules. The findings are schema v2 (`reading.schema` is `finding.v2`): each has a `code` from the issue-code catalog, `rooms`, and a `status` (`ok`, `done` or `none`) where it bills nothing. A row left out of the findings is named in `reading.notes` and counted in `counts.left_out`.

**Key required.** Send a connector key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`; free from `POST /v1/keys`). The web tool's page token is not accepted here. One document counts as one call of the key's daily free allowance, and a key can read 3 documents a day (UTC). Not on the x402 paid lane.

**Body.** `multipart/form-data` with the field `files` (one file, or up to 5 photos), or `application/json` `{"files": [{"name": "report.pdf", "content_base64": "..."}]}`. 15 MB a file, 25 MB an upload. Files with macros, scripts, embedded files or a password are refused.

**Privacy.** Upload a report (PDF, Word, Excel, CSV) or up to 5 photos, 5 pages at most. Pages are read by Microsoft Azure OpenAI. Please redact tenant names and signatures. Our server opens the file in an isolated converter, which turns each page into a plain image and drops everything else in the file. The page images are sent to Microsoft Azure OpenAI (run by Microsoft for us inside its US data zone) to copy out the findings and the unit facts; it is told not to copy names, addresses, phone numbers or signatures, and we remove any that slip through. The rows it copies are then sent as text, with contact details removed, to the same model, which codes them from the issue-code catalog. Nothing from the file is stored: the file, the page images and the text read from them are held in memory only while the request is processed. For up to a day we keep the answer for a page in memory, found by a one-way hash of the page image, so the same page gets the same answer. Prices are always worked out by our own rules, never by the AI model. How we handle uploads: /privacy#document-upload.

Alternative.title: Alternative
Alternative.description:
A different deadline when a condition holds (e.g. 14 days when nothing is deducted).

``condition`` is the statute's case in words. The engine evaluates it when ``requires``
lists mapped conditions, when the condition itself is one (``no_deductions``), or when an
effective-date window is the whole condition; any other alternative keeps the base rule and
adds an assumption naming it. ``combine`` says how a matching alternative applies:
``replace`` the base period (the first match wins), or take the ``later_date`` /
``earlier_date`` of the base deadline and this one (Connecticut: 21 days after the end of
the tenancy or 15 days after the forwarding address, whichever is later).

BrokenLease.title: BrokenLease
BrokenLease.description:
A tenant who moves out before the lease's scheduled end, without legal cause, does not end
the lease by leaving: it ends when the unit is re-rented or the term expires, whichever comes
first (New Jersey: NJ DCA, Truth in Renting, citing Mitchell v. First Real Estate Equities,
287 N.J. Super. 546 (App. Div. 1996); TEKTOLO-923). With no end date given, the return clock
starts at the scheduled end (a re-rental before it is the row's own alternative), and the
move-out is listed as the earlier date if a surrender was accepted.

CleaningRule.title: CleaningRule
CleaningRule.description:
How the statute treats a cleaning charge (a line's ``cleaning_kind``: ``beyond_wear``,
``routine`` or unknown).

``basis``: ``named`` when the deposit statute names cleaning as a purpose (to return the unit
to its move-in cleanliness, reasonable cleaning): unknown kind is 'yes' with the limit noted;
``damage`` when it does not, but a unit left dirtier than normal use is recoverable as damage
beyond normal wear, a breach of the tenant's duty to keep it clean, or a lease charge: unknown
kind is 'depends'. ``routine`` (cleaning after ordinary use): ``barred`` ('no': it is normal
wear) or ``lease`` ('depends': only if the lease provides it and the statute lets lease charges
come out of the deposit) or ``reasonable`` ('depends': the statute allows reasonable cleaning
costs with no wear limit, Mississippi, Nevada, Rhode Island, Utah). ``condition``: a precondition (Montana's written notice and 24 hours
to clean), checked against ``documentation.cleaning_notice`` (unknown: 'depends'; no: 'no',
unless ``unless_no_notice`` and the tenant gave no notice of leaving). A change in the law is a
new step of ``DeductionRules.cleaning``, judged on the day the landlord deducts (Colorado
HB25-1249: ordinary uncleanliness is normal wear from 2026-01-01).

not list are 'depends' (the lease, reasonableness, mitigation), never a flat 'no' (round 3
R9: D-OH-06, F-NE-03).

DepositCap.title: DepositCap
DepositCap.description:
The statutory deposit limit, computed (round 2 class 9).

``effective_on`` / ``effective_by``: the cap applies to deposits collected (``collected``,
California AB 12), deposits required (``required``, Colorado), or leases entered into or renewed (``lease_signed``, Georgia,
Maryland) on or after the date; earlier ones keep ``before_months_rent`` (None: no cap) and
``before_furnished_months``. ``furnished_months``: the cap for a furnished unit (Kansas);
``furnished_exempt``: none for one (Delaware). ``max_rent_usd``: no cap above this rent
(Alaska $2,000). ``min_term_months``: only for leases of at least this term (Delaware: one
year); ``max_term_months``: only for shorter ones (New Mexico: under a year).
``later_months_rent`` from ``later_after_months`` into the tenancy (Pennsylvania: one month
from the second year). ``variant_months``: another limit under facts the request cannot
state (California small landlords 2, Connecticut 62+ 1, North Carolina month-to-month 1.5,
Portland last month's rent 1.5, ...): a deposit between the two is 'depends'.

and leaves a blank to fill in where none was given; a manager note names the duty.

new tenant takes possession (Tennessee 66-28-301(g); G846-TN-05). No input states the day the
damage was found, so the cutoff is computed and stated, never applied to a line.

finding.description: The finding's id (its page and quote are in its extraction).

row.description: The row as read: room, item, condition, comment, count.

Evidence-Output.title: Evidence
Evidence-Output.description:
Why one finding needs a check, beside it (scope's ``Finding`` takes no extra keys; its
page and quote are in its ``extraction``): send ``findings`` to scope, keep this to check
them.

ExcessRemedy.title: ExcessRemedy
ExcessRemedy.description:
A remedy for taking a deposit above the cap (Maryland 8-203(b)(3): up to three times the
extra amount charged, plus fees).

Exclusion.title: Exclusion
Exclusion.description:
A category the statute keeps out of the deposit (Delaware: damage correctable by painting
and ordinary cleaning): 'no', cited.

method.title: Method
method.description: ai: free text; ai_document: an upload's page.

quote.description: ai_document: the row's words, contacts masked.

cell.description: ai_document: the cell read; move_in bills nothing, a hazard there is Possible.

Extraction.title: Extraction
Extraction.description: How our AI reader read a finding; never changes the price.

ExtractionReview.title: ExtractionReview
ExtractionReview.description: A person's review of a finding read from a document.

Fallback.title: Fallback
Fallback.description:
A second date for the full refund when the statement is not given in time or none is
needed (Illinois 710/1(a): no statement for property damage within 30 days: the deposit in
full within 45 days of vacating; a rent-only withholding needs no statement). The statement's
own date stays ``itemization_by``.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: site, a specific tool, or an idea for a new tool.

capability.title: Capability
capability.description: Tool id when scope is tool.

page.title: Page
page.description: Path of the page the feedback is about.

email.title: Email
email.description: Only if you want a reply.

source.title: Source
source.description: Optional self-reported source; not verified provenance.

reporter.title: Reporter
reporter.description: Optional reporter type, for example human or agent; self-reported.

agent_name.title: Agent Name
agent_name.description: Optional agent label. Do not include personal details or secrets.

FeedbackIn.title: FeedbackIn
FeedbackIn.description: What the site, a tool or an idea box sends to ``POST /v1/feedback``.

id.description: Your id; defaults to f1, f2, ... in order.

code.title: Code
code.description: From property_turnover_issue_codes; general.manual_quote if none fits. Send it on every finding.

description.title: Description
description.description: Deprecated; send code, with the words in source_text.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: More words; never billed or coded from.

area_sq_ft.title: Area Sq Ft
area_sq_ft.description: Measured area in sq ft; wins over a derived size.

material.title: Material
material.description: The material as written, e.g. '9x9 vinyl tile'.

year_statement.description: A year said in passing ("built 1972"); never sets property.year_built.

repeat_of.title: Repeat Of
repeat_of.description: Id of an earlier finding this repeats in its own rooms ("same as above"); it bills.

source_text.title: Source Text
source_text.description: The original words. Scanned for hazards; never billed or coded from.

Finding.title: Finding
Finding.description: One observed condition, coded from the issue-code catalog.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: exact: a taxonomy code was given. alias: the description matched an alias. ai: an AI reader chose the code from free text (see confidence, model; needs_review). unmapped: nothing matched (a manual-quote line). not_billed: the description says there is no work ('no mold', 'faucet not leaking', 'fixed by tenant'), or names no condition at all (a heading, a date, a signature, a year built); no lines, no refer-out; the issue it names is in suggestions and the reason in not_billed_reason.

not_billed_reason.title: Not Billed Reason
not_billed_reason.description: resolution 'not_billed' only. none: says there is none ('no mold', 'mold: none'); ok: says it works or is fine; done: says it was already fixed or done; no_condition: names no condition, only a heading, small talk, a signature or the year built ('Unit 4B - Move-out inspection', 'Built 1972'), see match_note (contract 0.13.0, additive).

text.title: Text
text.description: The finding as given (description, else code), for tracing.

location.title: Location
location.description: Where, as shown on the lines.

match_note.title: Match Note
match_note.description: Set when the match left a fixture word unexplained: check this finding.

uncertain.title: Uncertain
uncertain.description: The description hedges ('mold?', 'maybe', 'possible'). Refer-outs from uncertain findings are check-first: they add a warning instead of holding phases.

suggestions.title: Suggestions
suggestions.description: Suggested codes with readable names, best first.

needs_review.title: Needs Review
needs_review.description: True when software read this finding from free text (resolution 'ai'): check it.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: resolution 'ai' only: the AI reader's confidence, 0 to 1.

confirmed.title: Confirmed
confirmed.description: Read by AI and confirmed by the person (sent with confirmed: true).

carpet_present.title: Carpet Present
carpet_present.description: Is there wall-to-wall carpet? Omit if unknown.

carpet_sq_ft.title: Carpet Sq Ft
carpet_sq_ft.description: Carpeted area; omit to assume 60% of the floor area.

FloorCoverings.title: FloorCoverings
FloorCoverings.description: What is on the floors. Drives the carpet-cleaning baseline and whole-unit carpet sizes.

Forfeiture.title: Forfeiture
Forfeiture.description:
A statute's consequence for a missed duty: the landlord loses the right to keep some or
all of the deposit. Computed, not relayed: when the trigger is met as of ``as_of`` (the date
passed and the statement or refund was not sent in time, or a statement sent now would be
late), the barred lines become ``allowed: no`` (``depends`` when ``gate`` needs a finding or
the category is ``contested``) and the totals are recomputed. Before then the lines stand and
a warning names the date. ``not_in_input`` rows turn on facts the request cannot state and
are relayed as unknowns whenever something is deducted.

trigger.title: Trigger
trigger.description: late_statement, late_return, late_statement_or_return, late_claim_notice, late_action_or_return (Michigan 554.613), missing_documentation (a required receipt or photo is missing), receipts_after_estimate (paid receipts owed after an estimate not furnished in time) or not_in_input (facts the request cannot state).

status.title: Status
status.description: met: the date passed without the statement or refund (or sending it now would be late), so the barred lines are not counted; not_yet: still time; complied: sent on time; not_started: the clock has not started; relieved: the statute excuses the duty here; unknown: turns on facts you did not give.

due_by.title: Due By
due_by.description: The date the duty had to be met by.

court_rule_due_by.title: Court Rule Due By
court_rule_due_by.description: Missed by due_by on the plain count, but a court rule whose reach is unsettled (Florida's Rule 2.514) would run the period to this day; never applied. Omitted when no such rule extends it.

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: all: every deduction; damage: damage and cleaning only.

gate.title: Gate
gate.description: none, or the finding needed first (bad_faith, ...).

amount_released_usd.title: Amount Released Usd
amount_released_usd.description: What those lines would otherwise have kept from the deposit.

keeps_claim.title: Keeps Claim
keeps_claim.description: The charges can still be sued for separately.

ForfeitureCheck.title: ForfeitureCheck
ForfeitureCheck.description: A statute's forfeiture of the right to withhold, checked against the request.

Guide.title: Guide
Guide.description: An official plain-language resource for the state or city (an agency guide).

required.title: Required
required.description: None: depends on facts you did not give.

rate_percent.title: Rate Percent
rate_percent.description: Percent per year (the move-out rate when rates change).

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: What the rate applies to: deposit, or the excess (Ohio).

base_usd.title: Base Usd
base_usd.description: The amount the rate applies to.

parts.title: Parts
parts.description: Per-period amounts when the rate changed.

if_required_usd.title: If Required Usd
if_required_usd.description: The amount owed if the condition holds (a rent ordinance's interest when coverage is not known); not in the refund.

InterestPart.title: InterestPart
InterestPart.description: One period of an interest computation at one rate (a year, a rate window).

group.title: Group
group.description: The part of the unit it belongs to, for the group filter.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the code covers, in plain words.

not_when.title: Not When
not_when.description: When not to use it, in plain words.

rooms.title: Rooms
rooms.description: The rooms it is for; empty means any room.

default_extent.title: Default Extent
default_extent.description: spot | partial | full, used when a finding sends none.

refer_out.title: Refer Out
refer_out.description: The refer-out (licensed pro or compliance step) this code raises, if any.

examples.title: Examples
examples.description: Notes this code is for, as inspectors write them.

IssueCode.title: IssueCode
IssueCode.description:
One catalog entry. The short list carries code, name, group, default_extent and, where
the code has them, refer_out and rooms; a search hit (``q``) carries every field. Fields with
nothing to say are left out of the JSON.

client_refs.title: Client Refs
client_refs.description: Your own reference ids (e.g. unit_id, job_id). Echoed back, never used.

q.title: Q
q.description: Words to search for in the codes, names, aliases, descriptions and examples, e.g. 'pet stain carpet'. Hits come back with full detail. Leave out to list every code in short form.

group.title: Group
group.description: Only codes in this group, e.g. 'flooring' or 'walls' (a part of the unit, not a room). `groups` in the answer lists them all.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Most codes to return. Default: 8 with q, every code without.

include_aliases.title: Include Aliases
include_aliases.description: Also return aliases in the short list (search hits always carry them).

query.title: Query
query.description: Older name for q; use q.

area.title: Area
area.description: Older name for group; use group.

total_matches.title: Total Matches
total_matches.description: Codes matching q and group, before limit.

groups.title: Groups
groups.description: Every group, for the group filter.

areas.title: Areas
areas.description: Older name for groups (the same list).

manual_quote_code.title: Manual Quote Code
manual_quote_code.description: The code to send when no code fits; the line is quoted by hand.

city.title: City
city.description: The city you sent, as given.

city_overlay.title: City Overlay
city_overlay.description: The covered city whose rules were layered on, if any.

verified.title: Verified
verified.description: True when the main rule text was read verbatim at the official source and, when a city was given, the city's own rules are covered.

city_rules_checked.title: City Rules Checked
city_rules_checked.description: True: the city's overlay was applied; false: the city you gave is not covered, so only the state rule is shown (a local ordinance may be stricter); null: no city given.

LateFeeRule.title: LateFeeRule
LateFeeRule.description:
The most a late fee may be, per late payment (or per month), computed from the monthly
rent: ``flat_usd`` and ``percent`` (of the rent, or of the rent above ``over_usd``) combined
as the greater, the lesser or the sum; ``rent_tiers`` / ``unit_tiers`` pick the figure by
rent or building size. ``presumption``: the figure is only a safe harbor (Texas), so a larger
fee is 'depends'. ``conditional``: no figure can be checked (Massachusetts: nothing until 30
days late; Oregon's reasonable flat fee; Wisconsin's nonstandard provision): 'depends' with
the text. The engine allows up to the cap for one late payment unless the line says how many
(``late_payments``); more than one cap without a count is 'depends'.

LeaseAuthorized.title: LeaseAuthorized
LeaseAuthorized.description:
Deductions the statute allows only when the rental agreement authorizes applying the
deposit to them (California 1950.5(b)(4)). ``categories``: always conditional; ``replace``:
lines entered as ``other`` with ``work_kind: replace`` (a furnishing not returned) get the same
note. No input states the lease clause, so the lines are 'depends'.

LeaseBreakRule.title: LeaseBreakRule

Location.title: Location
Location.description: Where; a plain string works too.

MoveInPhotos.title: MoveInPhotos
MoveInPhotos.description:
Photos at the start of the tenancy, for tenancies beginning on or after ``tenancy_from``
(California 1950.5(g)(1): 2025-07-01). Checked against ``documentation.photos_move_in``.

MoveInStatement.title: MoveInStatement
MoveInStatement.description:
A written move-in condition statement or checklist the statute ties damage deductions to,
checked against ``documentation.move_in_condition_statement`` (Montana 70-25-206(3): without
it, damage and cleaning only on clear and convincing evidence: 'depends'; Washington
59.18.260(5): liable for the whole deposit: ``bars``, ``scope: all``).

MoveOutList.title: MoveOutList
MoveOutList.description:
A move-out inspection and damage list due a number of business days after the tenancy
ends and the tenant vacates (Georgia 44-7-33(b): three business days), checked against
``documentation.move_out_list``; dated, with a due-soon warning.

NotIfAbandoned.title: NotIfAbandoned
NotIfAbandoned.description:
The return rule does not apply when the tenant abandons (Louisiana 9:3251(C)): decided by
``tenant_abandoned`` (else no proper notice or a move-out before the end of the tenancy).

larger_than_body_pt.title: Larger Than Body Pt
larger_than_body_pt.description: At least this many points larger than the body text.

NoticeRelief.title: NoticeRelief
NoticeRelief.description:
The relief behind ``Forfeiture.tenant_notice_relief`` in the subsection's own words
(Florida 83.49(5)), quoted by the engine. On the row, so a ``history`` entry carries the
earlier wording for tenancies that ended before an amendment (ch. 2025-16: "written lease",
"shall relieve"; TEKTOLO-919).

child_under_6.title: Child Under 6
child_under_6.description: A child under 6 lives there or is expected to.

elderly.title: Elderly
elderly.description: Housing for the elderly (62+) or disabled; not just an older tenant.

Occupants.title: Occupants
Occupants.description: property.occupants: lead-rule facts about the unit; leave out what is unknown.

obligation_mode.title: Obligation Mode
obligation_mode.description: all: simultaneous duties; alternative: mutually exclusive full-refund or deduction-notice paths while deductions are unknown. For alternatives status says whether any path remains open; next_due is still the earliest conservative date.

refund_min_usd.title: Refund Min Usd
refund_min_usd.description: The refund if every 'depends' line is kept.

interest_usd.title: Interest Usd
interest_usd.description: Interest owed and computed; None when interest is owed but not computed (see interest_unknown) or not owed.

interest_unknown.title: Interest Unknown
interest_unknown.description: Interest is (or may be) owed but its amount is not computed.

returned_usd.title: Returned Usd
returned_usd.description: Already returned to the tenant (returned.amount_usd; the deposit for a full refund with no amount; 0 for nothing); None when not said or not given.

owed_now_usd.title: Owed Now Usd
owed_now_usd.description: Still owed to the tenant: refund_due_usd minus returned_usd, never below 0 (None when the amount returned is not known, or when required interest is still owed but not computed: see the interest_still_owed warning).

next_due.title: Next Due
next_due.description: The earliest open step's last day (what to act on first).

uncertain.title: Uncertain
uncertain.description: What the answer still turns on, in words.

Outcome.title: Outcome
Outcome.description:
The one answer every other section is worded from: what is owed to the tenant now, by
when, and what is still uncertain.

OverCapPenalty.title: OverCapPenalty
OverCapPenalty.description:
A fixed penalty per violation for a late fee above the limit, quoted (Colorado
38-12-105(3): $50 for each violation; 105(5)(b): $150 to $1,000 for each violation, after
the landlord fails to cure within seven days of notice). ``conditional``: it needs a step or
a finding the input cannot show (notice and no cure, a court).

PaymentMethod.title: PaymentMethod
PaymentMethod.description:
How the balance is paid changes the duty (``returned.method``, round 5 G-MI-01).
``electronic_after_notice``: an electronic balance may follow a timely notice of damages by
``days`` (Michigan 554.609(3), 2026 PA 102: a check goes with the notice); with the method
unknown the later date is an alternative. ``electronic_if_paid_electronically``: the balance
goes back electronically when the deposit or rent was paid that way, unless agreed otherwise
in writing (California 1950.5 as amended by AB 414): a check is warned about.

not_applicable_reason.title: Not Applicable Reason
not_applicable_reason.description: Facts that rule out this monetary remedy. When present, estimated_max_usd is zero; this does not say whether a deposit remains held or owed.

in_addition_to_refund.title: In Addition To Refund
in_addition_to_refund.description: The damages come on top of returning the amount withheld (Ohio, West Virginia), not instead of it.

fees_only_without_multiple.title: Fees Only Without Multiple
fees_only_without_multiple.description: Attorney's fees go to the prevailing party except where the multiple is awarded (Idaho 6-324): the multiple with no fees, or actual damages plus fees, never both. Shown only when true.

estimated_min_usd.title: Estimated Min Usd
estimated_min_usd.description: The least of the readings when the statute's base is unsettled (a refund paid late, 'depends' lines, IL's 'deposit due'); None when it is the same as the max.

base.title: Base
base.description: What a multiple of the amount withheld is taken of: withheld, wrongfully_withheld, entitled_balance or exceeds_damages.

estimated_max_usd.title: Estimated Max Usd
estimated_max_usd.description: fixed + multiple x basis amount (with any floor or cap); exposure, not a verdict. None when the basis is unknown (monthly rent not given).

forfeits_right_to_withhold.title: Forfeits Right To Withhold
forfeits_right_to_withhold.description: True: a late statement or refund takes away the right to withhold with no court finding; None: it does only on a finding (bad faith, willful, unreasonable); False: the statute states no such forfeiture.

additional.description: City penalties in addition to the state's (not included in its estimate).

RateWindow.description:

month, a Connecticut calendar year), as the ``rules`` result shows one step of

ReadDocumentResponse.description: The API's answer to a document: a reading, never an estimate.

findings.title: Findings
findings.description: Every finding the rules answered, in the shape the rules operation accepts.

notes.description: What the reading noticed while reading the text.

Reading.description:

operation to get a verified answer.

parser.title: Parser
parser.description: Findings the deterministic parser and matcher placed, or sent coded.

ReadingNote.title: ReadingNote
ReadingNote.description: Something the reading noticed (a range, a room read from the words, a year built).

ReferOutHint.title: ReferOutHint
ReferOutHint.description:
A possible safety item named in a finding's words or matched item. A hint only: scope
decides, and lists the refer-out in its answer.

unconfirmed.title: Unconfirmed
unconfirmed.description: No finding confirms it: every finding that raised it was hedged ('maybe', '?'), named the hazard only in its words (description, notes or location label) rather than through its issue code, or stated an older year built than the request. state.description: US state, 2-letter code (e.g. 'CA'); a state name also works.

city.description: City, for a city overlay where covered (e.g. 'Chicago'). Optional.

monthly_rent_usd.title: Monthly Rent Usd
monthly_rent_usd.description: Monthly rent, for the deposit cap check.

building_units.title: Building Units
building_units.description: Units in the building. Some interest rules depend on it (NY 6+, IL 25+).

move_in_on.title: Move In On
move_in_on.description: Tenancy start (YYYY-MM-DD). Used for interest and, when an item's age is unknown, for depreciation.

tenancy_ended_on.title: Tenancy Ended On
tenancy_ended_on.description: When the tenancy actually ended (YYYY-MM-DD): the lease's end, or an earlier termination or accepted surrender. Deadlines that run from the end of the tenancy use it. For a tenant who left before the lease was due to end, send the scheduled end as lease_end_on (older callers sent it here, which still works: the deadline is then counted from it, with the move-out date as an earlier alternative where the facts point to one).
tenancy_ended_on.x-mcp-description: Actual tenancy end: lease end, early termination or accepted surrender (YYYY-MM-DD). End-of-tenancy deadlines use this; send a different scheduled end as lease_end_on. Legacy scheduled ends still work, with an earlier move-out alternative where applicable.

lease_end_on.title: Lease End On
lease_end_on.description: Day the lease was scheduled to end (YYYY-MM-DD), when it differs from when the tenancy actually ended (a broken lease). Lost rent and lease-break charges run to it; deadlines do not (they follow tenancy_ended_on, else the move-out, with the scheduled end as a later alternative).

vacated_on.title: Vacated On
vacated_on.description: Day the tenant moved out and returned possession (YYYY-MM-DD).

forwarding_address_received_on.title: Forwarding Address Received On
forwarding_address_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's written forwarding address (YYYY-MM-DD). Several states start or hold the clock on it (Texas, Connecticut, Iowa, Minnesota).
forwarding_address_received_on.x-mcp-description: Written forwarding address received (YYYY-MM-DD). Can start/hold clocks in TX, CT, IA, MN.

tenant_gave_forwarding_address.title: Tenant Gave Forwarding Address
tenant_gave_forwarding_address.description: False if no written forwarding address was ever given. IL, PA, OH, SC and NH may relieve the penalty; Delaware also accepts a tenant notice address in the lease. Implied true by forwarding_address_received_on.
tenant_gave_forwarding_address.x-mcp-description: False: no written forwarding address ever given. May relieve penalties in IL/PA/OH/SC/NH; DE also accepts a lease notice address. forwarding_address_received_on implies true.

demand_received_on.title: Demand Received On
demand_received_on.description: Day you received the tenant's demand for the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD; written in Oklahoma, by first-class mail in Maryland 8-203(h)). Arizona, Kansas, Oklahoma, South Carolina and Mississippi start the clock on it.
demand_received_on.x-mcp-description: Deposit demand received (YYYY-MM-DD): written in OK; first-class mail in MD (8-203(h)). Starts clocks in AZ/KS/OK/SC/MS.

new_tenant_moved_in_on.title: New Tenant Moved In On
new_tenant_moved_in_on.description: Day a new tenant moved in, if the unit was re-rented (YYYY-MM-DD). West Virginia and Wisconsin can end the period earlier; rent claimed for days from it on is not recoverable (re-rent mitigation).
new_tenant_moved_in_on.x-mcp-description: Re-rented: new tenant's move-in date (YYYY-MM-DD). Can shorten WV/WI periods; rent overlapping the new tenancy is unrecoverable.

new_tenant_rent_usd.title: New Tenant Rent Usd
new_tenant_rent_usd.description: Monthly rent the new tenant pays (with new_tenant_moved_in_on): the rent received for overlapping days is credited against rent claimed for them.

statement_sent_on.title: Statement Sent On
statement_sent_on.description: Day you sent (or delivered) the itemized statement (YYYY-MM-DD). With it the statement is judged on time or late; documentation.itemized_statement alone cannot tell.
statement_sent_on.x-mcp-description: Itemized statement sent/delivered (YYYY-MM-DD), to assess timeliness; documentation.itemized_statement alone supplies no date.

claim_notice_sent_on.title: Claim Notice Sent On
claim_notice_sent_on.description: Day you sent the written notice of intent to impose a claim on the deposit (YYYY-MM-DD). Florida (due within 30 days of termination) and the District of Columbia (within 45 days): the balance is due 30 days after it; a late notice does not count.
claim_notice_sent_on.x-mcp-description: Written claim notice sent (YYYY-MM-DD). FL: within 30 days of termination; DC:45. Balance due 30 days after timely notice; late notice does not count.

lease_return_days.title: Lease Return Days
lease_return_days.description: Return period the lease sets, in days, where the statute lets a lease set one (Colorado up to 60, Idaho up to 30, Maine shorter).

tenant_gave_proper_notice.title: Tenant Gave Proper Notice
tenant_gave_proper_notice.description: A termination notice that meets the statute was given (Alaska: 14 days instead of 30 when nothing is deducted for damage).

interest_paid_through.title: Interest Paid Through
interest_paid_through.description: Interest already paid or credited to the tenant up to this day (annual-payment rules: San Francisco, Los Angeles, Berkeley, Connecticut, Massachusetts, ...): interest is counted from it.
interest_paid_through.x-mcp-description: Interest already paid/credited through this date; accrual starts here (annual-payment rules, e.g. SF/LA/Berkeley/CT/MA).

nonstandard_provision_signed.title: Nonstandard Provision Signed
nonstandard_provision_signed.description: Wisconsin: the tenant signed a separate NONSTANDARD RENTAL PROVISIONS document covering the charge (ATCP 134.06(3)(b)); false makes such charges 'no'.

pet_deposit_usd.title: Pet Deposit Usd
pet_deposit_usd.description: The part of deposit_usd that is a pet deposit (outside the cap in Missouri, Alabama, North Dakota and Saint Paul; allowed on top of it up to one month in Hawaii and Alaska, half a month in Kansas, a quarter in Nebraska).
pet_deposit_usd.x-mcp-description: Pet portion of deposit_usd: outside caps in MO/AL/ND/Saint Paul; extra cap allowance of 1 month in HI/AK, half in KS, quarter in NE.

tenant_age_62_plus.title: Tenant Age 62 Plus
tenant_age_62_plus.description: The tenant is 62 or older (Connecticut: a one-month cap).

tenant_age_60_plus.title: Tenant Age 60 Plus
tenant_age_60_plus.description: A person 60 or older occupies the unit (New Hampshire 540-A:5, I: the owner-occupied exemption does not reach the unit). tenant_age_62_plus true implies it.
tenant_age_60_plus.x-mcp-description: An occupant is 60+ (NH 540-A:5,I: owner-occupied exemption excluded). tenant_age_62_plus=true implies this.

third_party_managed.description: A third party manages the unit or collects rent for a fee.

owner_is_natural_person.description: Georgia only (44-7-36): the units are owned by a natural person (false: an LLC, corporation, partnership or trust owns them). The small-landlord exemption reaches only a natural person; not given, the statute is shown with the exemption as the alternative.

deposit_in_separate_account.title: Deposit In Separate Account
deposit_in_separate_account.description: Tennessee only (66-28-301(a)): the deposit was kept in a separate account used only for deposits. No account and no damage listing means none of it can be kept (66-28-301(c)).

renter_notice_served_on.title: Renter Notice Served On
renter_notice_served_on.description: Utah only (YYYY-MM-DD): day the renter served the 57-17-3(3) notice after the deadline passed. The owner then has five business days to comply (57-17-3(5)); without the notice there is no relief under 57-17-5.

landlord_filed_action_on.description: Michigan only (YYYY-MM-DD): day the landlord sued for the damages claimed (554.613: sue or return the balance within 45 days). Not given: no suit assumed.
landlord_filed_action_on.x-mcp-description: MI 554.613: date landlord sued for claimed damage (YYYY-MM-DD); sue or return balance within 45 days. Omitted assumes no suit.

prepaid_rent_usd.description: Rent paid in advance beyond the first month, held besides deposit_usd. Counts toward the cap in AK, AZ, CA, CT, MD, MI and NY; earns interest in CT, MA (last month's rent), MD and Chicago; in Minneapolis it lowers the deposit cap to half a month. In UT its balance is returned with the deposit and counted in the refund (57-17-3(2)(b)): send only the unused part (rent already applied to a rental period is not a balance). Elsewhere the refund covers the deposit only and a warning says unused prepaid rent is owed back too.

colorado_post_closing_occupancy.description: Colorado: buyer-landlord bought this residence from seller-tenant; both executed purchase-contract post-closing occupancy before the deposit was required. True confirms all facts; false excludes; null unknown. Exception from 2027-01-01.

lease_signed_or_renewed_on.title: Lease Signed Or Renewed On
lease_signed_or_renewed_on.description: Day the current lease was signed or last renewed (YYYY-MM-DD). Georgia (2024-07-01) and Maryland (2024-10-01) caps apply to leases from then; defaults to move_in_on, with a warning that a later renewal may bring the new cap.
lease_signed_or_renewed_on.x-mcp-description: Current lease signing/last renewal (YYYY-MM-DD). GA cap from 2024-07-01; MD from 2024-10-01. Defaults move_in_on; warns later renewal may activate cap.

lease_term_months.description: Term of the lease in months (0 for month-to-month). Delaware's cap applies to leases of a year or more, New Mexico's to shorter ones.

furnished.title: Furnished
furnished.description: The unit is rented furnished (California before AB 12: 3 months; Kansas: 1.5 months; Delaware: no cap).

rent_ordinance_covered.description: The unit is covered by the city's rent ordinance (Los Angeles RSO, Berkeley Rent Ordinance). Their deposit interest is owed only then; unknown: the amount is shown beside the refund, not in it.
rent_ordinance_covered.x-mcp-description: Covered by LA RSO or Berkeley Rent Ordinance: required for their deposit interest. Unknown interest stays beside, not inside, refund.

text.description: Draft itemized statement, plain text, no names or addresses, with every note for both audiences (the manager's full draft; see notes for which is which).

done_on.title: Done On

days_late.title: Days Late
days_late.description: Days after due_by (late, or overdue as of as_of).

UnsettledRollover.title: UnsettledRollover
UnsettledRollover.description:
A time-computation rule that may reach the state's periods but whose reach is unsettled
(TEKTOLO-897, gate v33-896 V33-FL-08: Florida's 83.49 states no method of computing time, and
Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.514(a) covers "any ... statute that does not specify a
method of computing time", but it is a court rule and a landlord's notice is given out of
court). Never applied to a date: the unmoved day stays the one to act by. A claim notice
sent on a day only the rule would reach makes the claim 'depends'; a refund then is shown late
(the safe reading) with a warning; the rule is quoted either way.

``start_rolls``: counting begins on the next day that is not a Saturday, Sunday or legal
holiday (2.514(a)(1)(A)); the last day then moves past one too ((1)(C)). ``holidays``: the
legal holidays it names, by their name in the federal list (``Day after Thanksgiving`` is the
Friday after it), observed on the Friday before a Saturday and the Monday after a Sunday.

UnsettledStart.title: UnsettledStart
UnsettledStart.description:
A start event the statute's words leave open between two readings (TEKTOLO-939, gate
v35-935 V35-FL-11/13: Florida 83.49(3)(a) before ch. 2025-16 ran both periods "Upon the
vacating of the premises for termination of the lease", which leaves open whether a move-out
before the lease ended starts them or the lease's termination does). The return rule's own
``start`` leads; this is the other reading. Only when it falls later is it used: the dates it
gives are listed as alternatives, and a notice of claim late on the leading reading but on
time on this one makes the claim 'depends'. Never applied to a date.

``later_text_on``: a later text of the section, in force from this day, counts from this
reading's event (Florida ch. 2025-16, from 2025-07-01: "within 30 days after the termination
of the rental agreement"); a notice given on or after it may be judged by that text, which
``later_text_note`` explains.

UtilityLimit.title: UtilityLimit
UtilityLimit.description:
Utility charges the statute lets the landlord deduct, by kind (Massachusetts: water only).
A utility line is 'yes' for these kinds, 'no' for others, 'depends' when the kind is not
given (``utility_kind`` on the line).

code.title: Code
code.description: A verify code, or a whole verify link (…/verify/<code>).

text.title: Text
text.description: Optional, for a summary's code: the summary's text, to check it was not changed. Compared in memory and not stored.

jws.title: Jws
jws.description: Instead of a code: an API result's signature.jws, to check its signature.

verified.title: Verified
verified.description: True only when Tektolo's signature checks out.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Empty when verified; else malformed, unsupported, unknown_key, bad_signature or signing_off.

tool_name.title: Tool Name
tool_name.description: The web tool's name when a web tool issued it.

document.title: Document
document.description: What the code was printed on.

covers.title: Covers
covers.description: What the code's keyed digest covers: one result, or a summary's text.

WtpAnswer.title: WtpAnswer
WtpAnswer.description: Optional price evidence, never a quoted offer or a payment instruction.

year.title: Year
year.description: Left out when the words name none ('Victorian').

YearStatement.title: YearStatement
YearStatement.description: When the words say it was built.

rules_as_of.title: Rules As Of
rules_as_of.description: The rules are as of this day: the earliest date on which a source behind this answer was read (the accessed date of each source in sources; each citation gives its own). A change in the law after it is not reflected unless a later ruleset version says so: every version and what it changed is listed at /changelog, with an Atom feed per state. Null when no state's rules apply (a state not covered).

allowed_usd.title: Allowed Usd
allowed_usd.description: Sum of lines with allowed = yes.

depends_usd.title: Depends Usd
depends_usd.description: Sum of 'depends' lines at the amount the rule would allow if they stand (not in allowed_usd or the refund).

interest_usd.title: Interest Usd
interest_usd.description: Interest credited (0 when none is owed; null when interest is or may be owed but its amount is not computed, so it is not in the refund).

counted_floor_usd.title: Counted Floor Usd
counted_floor_usd.description: The certain minimum of the 'depends' lines (their least amount on every reading), counted in the refund and itemized on the statement as its own deduction. The statement's total deductions are allowed_usd + counted_floor_usd.

refund_due_usd.title: Refund Due Usd
refund_due_usd.description: deposit + interest - allowed - counted_floor, never below 0.

tenant_owes_usd.title: Tenant Owes Usd
tenant_owes_usd.description: Allowed deductions above deposit + interest (collect separately).

refund_min_usd.title: Refund Min Usd
refund_min_usd.description: The refund if every 'depends' line stands: deposit + interest - allowed - depends, never below 0. Equals refund_due_usd when nothing depends.

rules_as_of.title: Rules As Of
rules_as_of.description: The oldest reading of the sources behind the legal items in this result (refer-outs and state mandates): the rules are as of this date. None when the result states no legal rule.

note.title: Note
note.default: must, should and could are work lines only. visit_charges (minimum call-out and trip fees, once per trade) are added on top: subtotal = must + should + could + visit_charges; total = subtotal + tax. allowances and to_confirm (uncertain items) are outside the total.

to_confirm.description: Lines from uncertain findings ('maybe', '?', 'possible') and safety items read from plain words (the refer-out safety net): priced, but outside every total until confirmed on site. Those lines carry to_confirm: true (contract 0.7.0).

allowances.description: Budget allowance for quote-required lines (refer-outs, manual quotes). Shown outside the totals: subtotal and total never include it.
